stem: In an acute-care hospital, a client has an infected wound with a target multidrug-resistant organism (MDRO) and drainage that is not fully contained by the dressing. Which precautions should the nurse implement?

options.D: Standard Precautions only, with no additional transmission-based precautions

rationale: CDC recommends Standard Precautions for all patient encounters and, in acute-care hospitals, routine Contact Precautions for patients infected or colonized with target MDROs. Contact Precautions also apply when excessive or uncontained wound drainage increases environmental contamination and transmission risk. Therefore A is the best answer. Airborne or Droplet Precautions are not indicated solely by the scenario described.
educational_objective: Apply Contact Precautions in addition to Standard Precautions for an acute-care client with a target MDRO and uncontained draining wound.
source_organization: Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC)
source_document_title: Management of Multidrug-Resistant Organisms in Healthcare Settings — Summary of Recommendations; Isolation Precautions
source_version_date: CDC pages updated 2024; current pages accessed 2026-08-17

source_claim_supported: In acute care, target-MDRO infection warrants Contact Precautions in addition to Standard Precautions; uncontained/excessive wound drainage independently supports Contact Precautions because of transmission risk.

correction_summary: Added the acute-care setting and specified a target MDRO with uncontained drainage so the Contact-Precautions recommendation is not incorrectly generalized to all care settings. Replaced vague 'combination of precautions tailored to risk' with the exact Standard-plus-Contact action.
audit_findings: A directly matches CDC acute-care guidance. B and C introduce transmission modes not established in the stem; D omits the indicated Contact Precautions. The setting qualifier removes the LTCF/ambulatory/home-care exception ambiguity. No second answer, cueing or unresolved conflict remains.
